title: Young woman, chest tightness and tingling (panic attack)
tricky_aspects: AI should not jump to A, but ask the right questions

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: I think I'm having a heart attack, my heart is racing and my chest is tight!

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: Okay, I'm here. Where are you?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Home, Karl XII-gatan 9, Lund. I'm alone.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: How old are you? When did it start?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: I'm 24. Ten minutes ago, I was studying for an exam tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Yes really fast. And my hands and lips are tingling, my fingers are cramping.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: Does the chest pain go to your arm, jaw or back?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: No, it's just tight in the middle. It doesn't get worse when I move.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: Have you had anything like this before? Any heart problems, or medicines?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: I've had panic attacks before, last month. No heart problems. I don't take anything.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: Try to breathe slowly with me: in through the nose for four, out through the mouth for six.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Okay... it's getting a bit better. The tingling is less.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: Good. A nurse will call you back within a few minutes. If you get pain spreading to your arm, faint, or feel worse, call 112 again.
